newsitem.title: SIERRA LEONE: Alusuisse unit shipping 100,000T bauxite.
newsitem.headline: Alusuisse unit shipping 100,000T bauxite.

text.p: Sierra Leone's Sieromco, a subsidiary of Swiss aluminium manufacturer Alusuisse-Lonza Holding AG, said it had shipped 32,000 tonnes of Sierra Leone bauxite stockpiles to France in December and will move about 68,000 tonnes by next week. Managing Director James Westwood told Reuters all the shipment was for Pechiney, one of the world's four largest aluminiyum producers.
The Sierra Leone bauxite was processed before civil war and a 1995 attack on Sieremco's mine in the West African country closed the facility.
"We are selling the last bauxite stocks which were processed before the attack and we have done sufficient repairs in order to load the bauxite for shipment," Westwood said.

Sieromco, which until its closure in January 1995 provided a fifth of Sierra Leone's mineral export earnings, decided in 1996 not to reopen its bauxite mine at Mokanji in southern Sierra Leone. But it did not rule out the possibility of the mine being sold to another investor.

The company had lost an estimated $30 million in assets when the mine was attacked and looted and it decided it was not economically viable to reopen the mine, which has only 10 years of bauxite reserves left.
The government and rebels signed an accord on November 30 ending civil war which erupted in 1991 and devastated the country's mining-based economy.
Sierra Leone officials said three companies had shown some interest in buying the mine, but they gave no details of the potential investors.
